# Purpose {#sec-purpose}

The submitted paper (v1.0.0) conditions only on survey items asked *before* the games.
This notebook builds the analysis tibble for an exploratory extension that adds the substantive items asked *after* the games.
Post-game items are **correlates** of the Muslim penalty, not moderators.
Each respondent saw a random number of Muslim profiles, and that exposure could shift how they answered later items.
Every result built on these items is an exploratory addendum, not a main result.

The pipeline repeats `02_data_prep.qmd` step by step.
It applies the same respondent filters, the same wave-1 backfill, the same missingness rule, and the same listwise deletion.
@sec-reproduce checks that the pipeline, run with only the v1.0.0 variables, reproduces `eu25_long.rds` exactly.
The output is `data/02_processed/eu25_long_ext.rds` plus a variable dictionary `var_dict_ext.rds`.

# Setup {#sec-setup}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# execution time
start_time <- Sys.time()
# console width
options(width = 80)
# packages
p_required <- c(
  "tidyverse", # dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr etc
  "here", # to never worry about directories
  "knitr", # for kable()
  "broom", # tidy() model output
  "sandwich", # clustered vcov, contamination check
  "lmtest", # coeftest() with custom vcov
  "sessioninfo" # session docs
)
packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
p_to_install <- p_required[!(p_required %in% packages)]
if (length(p_to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(p_to_install)
}
sapply(p_required, require, character.only = TRUE)
rm(p_required, p_to_install, packages)
```

# Load data {#sec-load}

```{r}
#| label: load-data
eu25games2019 <- read_rds(here("data", "01_raw", "eu25games2019.rds"))
eu25_long_v1 <- read_rds(here("data", "02_processed", "eu25_long.rds"))
```

# Respondent filters {#sec-filters}

These are the filters from `02_data_prep.qmd`, in the same order.
The exploratory duplicate inspection there is not repeated.
Only the steps that change the sample are kept.

```{r}
#| label: filters
# pids who played at least one game wave
pids_in_games <- eu25games2019 |>
  filter(meta_wave %in% c(2, 3)) |>
  distinct(meta_pid) |>
  pull(meta_pid)

eu25games2019_clean <- eu25games2019 |>
  # n = 103,685 -> 70,685
  filter(meta_wave %in% c(2, 3) | meta_pid %in% pids_in_games) |>
  # n = 70,685 -> 41,457
  filter(der_att_check_3)

# duplicate-pid completers
to_remove <- eu25games2019_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(cj_dict1_pl2)) |>
  group_by(meta_wave, meta_pid) |>
  filter(meta_finished) |>
  count(meta_pid, sort = T) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  pull(meta_pid)

eu25games2019_clean2 <- eu25games2019_clean |>
  # n = 41,457 -> 36,912
  filter(meta_finished) |>
  # n = 36,912 -> 36,881
  filter(!(meta_pid %in% to_remove)) |>
  # n = 36,881 -> 35,235
  filter(meta_pid %in% meta_pid[meta_wave %in% c(2, 3)]) |>
  # n = 35,235 -> 35,212
  filter(!(meta_wave == 1 & meta_pid == "1078674746")) |>
  filter(!(meta_wave == 1 & meta_pid == "1277956255")) |>
  filter(!(meta_wave == 1 & meta_pid == "1516614375")) |>
  filter(!(meta_wave == 1 & is.na(meta_pid)))

stopifnot(nrow(eu25games2019_clean2) == 35212)
```

## Post-game items (new) {#sec-vars-post}

Candidates are the substantive items in the post-game blocks of the wave-2 and wave-3 questionnaires (`data/questionaire/W{2,3}_EU25_Survey_Ireland_basic.txt` in the [source repository](https://github.com/LS-Konig/eu25games2019)).
In both waves the post-game blocks come after the dictator and trust games.

```{r}
#| label: vars-post-game
vars_post_game <- c(
  # political interest
  "q_nat_int",
  "q_eu_int",
  # nativism
  "q_nativ_econ",
  "q_nativ_cult",
  # informed about EU institutions
  "q_eu_informed_com",
  "q_eu_informed_cou",
  "q_eu_informed_ep",
  "q_eu_informed_cjeu",
  # trust in EU institutions
  "q_eu_trust_com",
  "q_eu_trust_cou",
  "q_eu_trust_ep",
  "q_eu_trust_cjeu",
  # CJEU evaluation
  "q_cjeu_abolish",
  "q_cjeu_satisfaction",
  # economic evaluations
  "q_eval_econ_eur",
  "q_eval_econ_nat",
  "q_eval_fin_household",
  "q_eval_job",
  # satisfaction with democracy
  "q_satis_demo_nat",
  "q_satis_demo_eu",
  # ideology
  "q_lr_self",
  "q_euint_self",
  # risk and time preferences
  "q_risk_taking",
  "q_future_discount",
  # occupation
  "q_occ_current"
)

# eu knowledge (scored, see below)
vars_know <- paste0("q_eu_know_", 1:5)
```

Several post-game blocks are left out by design:

- **Feeling thermometers** (`q_thermo_1..6`) rate political parties. Each slot is a different party in each country, so a slot is not comparable across countries.
- **Party and institution placements** (`q_lr_party_*`, `q_euint_party_*`, `q_lr_com` etc.), **norms**, **globalization**, **national efficacy**, **news use**, and **vote ranking** items are each missing for more than 25% of game players.
- **`*_fra` variants** duplicate answers that French wave-2 respondents also gave to the main items. They add nothing.
- `q_region` (300 levels), `q_occ_last` (65% missing, asked only of non-workers), `q_cjeu_pos` (70% missing).

**EU knowledge.** Waves 2 and 3 ask *different* true/false questions under the same names `q_eu_know_1..5`.
The raw factors are therefore not comparable across waves, and they are not backfilled from wave 1.
Two wave-specific scores replace them: the number of correct answers on items 1–4, and the number of "don't know" answers on items 1–5.
Item 5 is a country-specific question about the national parliament or government, so it does not enter the correct-answer score.
The answer key comes from the questionnaire wording, given the survey dates (April–May 2019):

| Item | Wave 2 statement | Key | Wave 3 statement | Key |
|:---|:---|:---:|:---|:---:|
| 1 | Each Member State elects the same number of MEPs | False | The European Council is officially called the Council of the EU | False |
| 2 | Antonio Tajani is the current President of the European Commission | False | There are 1125 members in the European Parliament | False |
| 3 | The Council presidency is currently held by Romania | True | Vassilios Skouris is the current President of the CJEU | False |
| 4 | Only national courts decide whether national law is compatible with EU law | False | The Euro area currently consists of 19 Member States | True |

: EU knowledge answer key by wave. {#tbl-know-key}

```{r}
#| label: know-key
know_key <- tribble(
  ~meta_wave , ~item         , ~correct ,
           2 , "q_eu_know_1" , "False"  ,
           2 , "q_eu_know_2" , "False"  ,
           2 , "q_eu_know_3" , "True"   ,
           2 , "q_eu_know_4" , "False"  ,
           3 , "q_eu_know_1" , "False"  ,
           3 , "q_eu_know_2" , "False"  ,
           3 , "q_eu_know_3" , "False"  ,
           3 , "q_eu_know_4" , "True"
)
```

# Wave-1 backfill {#sec-backfill}

This is the backfill from `02_data_prep.qmd`, extended to the post-game items.
A missing wave-2/3 answer is filled with the same panelist's wave-1 answer, and existing values are never overwritten.
For post-game items a wave-1 answer is a pre-treatment measure, so the filled cells are, if anything, cleaner than the observed ones.
Items not asked in wave 1 are unaffected, because their wave-1 values are all missing.

```{r}
#| label: backfill
vars_backfill <- c(vars_pre_game, vars_post_game)

eu25games2019_selected <- eu25games2019_clean2 |>
  select(
    meta_wave,
    meta_country,
    meta_pid,
    all_of(vars_backfill),
    all_of(vars_know),
    starts_with("cj_attr"),
    starts_with("cj_treatment"),
    starts_with("cj_dict"),
    starts_with("cj_trust"),
    # postgame demographic vars only
    q_rural_urban,
    q_edu_age_stop
  )

# each panelist's w1 values
w1_values <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  filter(meta_wave == 1) |>
  select(meta_pid, meta_country, all_of(vars_backfill))

# na counts before backfill
na_before <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  filter(meta_wave %in% c(2, 3)) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(vars_backfill), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "na_before")

# backfill one variable
backfill_w1 <- function(df, v) {
  w1 <- paste0(v, "_w1")
  df |>
    mutate(
      "filled_{v}" := meta_wave %in%
        c(2, 3) &
        is.na(.data[[v]]) &
        !is.na(.data[[w1]])
    ) |>
    mutate("{v}" := coalesce(.data[[v]], .data[[w1]]))
}

eu25games2019_selected <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  left_join(
    w1_values,
    by = c("meta_pid", "meta_country"),
    suffix = c("", "_w1")
  ) |>
  reduce(vars_backfill, backfill_w1, .init = _) |>
  select(-ends_with("_w1"))

# cells filled
n_filled <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  filter(meta_wave %in% c(2, 3)) |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("filled_"), ~ sum(.x))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_filled") |>
  mutate(variable = str_remove(variable, "^filled_"))

eu25games2019_selected <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  select(-starts_with("filled_"))

fill_audit <- na_before |>
  left_join(n_filled, by = "variable") |>
  filter(n_filled > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_filled))

fill_audit |>
  kable(caption = "Wave-1 backfill: W2/W3 missing cells before, and cells filled.")
```

# Reproduce v1.0.0 {#sec-reproduce}

`to_long()` is the reshape and the display-aware profile covariates from `02_data_prep.qmd`, wrapped in a function.
Run on the v1.0.0 variable set, the pipeline must reproduce `eu25_long.rds` exactly.
This guards the extended tibble against any silent drift in the shared steps.

```{r}
#| label: to-long
to_long <- function(wide) {
  wide |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -c(
        starts_with("meta_"),
        starts_with("q_"),
        starts_with("cj_attr"),
        starts_with("cj_treatment"),
        starts_with("der_eu_know"),
        contains("_instr_")
      ),
      names_to = c("game_type", "round", ".value"),
      names_pattern = "^(cj_dict|cj_trust)(\\d+)_(.+)$"
    ) |>
    rename_with(
      ~ paste0("cj_", .),
      -c(
        starts_with("meta_"),
        starts_with("q_"),
        starts_with("cj_attr"),
        starts_with("cj_treatment"),
        starts_with("der_eu_know"),
        contains("_instr_")
      )
    ) |>
    mutate(
      # eu stance shown -> 1,3
      der_cj_eu_identity = case_when(
        grepl("eustance", cj_treatment) & cj_eupos == "eu_citizen" ~
          "eu_citizen",
        grepl("eustance", cj_treatment) & cj_eupos == "not_eu_citizen" ~
          "not_eu_citizen",
        !grepl("eustance", cj_treatment) ~ "not_displayed"
      ),
      # party shown -> 1,2; conational suppressed -> 4 & own_country
      der_cj_partisanship = case_when(
        grepl("partisan", cj_treatment) ~ "shown",
        cj_treatment == "4_somenat" &
          cj_nationality_shown == "own_country" ~ "not_shown",
        .default = "not_applicable"
      )
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: reproduce-v1
eu25_long_repro <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  select(-all_of(c(vars_post_game, vars_know, vars_pre_dropped))) |>
  na.omit() |>
  to_long()

stopifnot(
  nrow(eu25_long_repro) == 169206,
  setequal(names(eu25_long_repro), names(eu25_long_v1)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    eu25_long_repro,
    select(eu25_long_v1, all_of(names(eu25_long_repro))),
    check.attributes = FALSE
  ))
)
cat("v1.0.0 analysis tibble reproduced exactly.\n")
```

# Recode post-game items {#sec-recode}

Risk-taking and time-preference answers are stored as translated strings that start with the scale point, e.g. "(1) Completely unwilling…".
The leading number is the 1–7 scale value.
The two knowledge scores are computed per wave from @tbl-know-key.

```{r}
#| label: recode-post
# leading scale point
scale_point <- function(x) as.integer(str_extract(x, "(?<=^\\()\\d+(?=\\))"))

know_scores <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  filter(meta_wave %in% c(2, 3)) |>
  select(meta_wave, meta_pid, all_of(vars_know)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(vars_know), names_to = "item", values_to = "answer") |>
  left_join(know_key, by = c("meta_wave", "item")) |>
  summarise(
    # all five answered?
    know_complete = all(!is.na(answer)),
    der_eu_know_correct = sum(as.character(answer) == correct, na.rm = TRUE),
    der_eu_know_dk = sum(as.character(answer) == "Don't Know", na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(meta_wave, meta_pid)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    der_eu_know_correct = if_else(know_complete, der_eu_know_correct, NA),
    der_eu_know_dk = if_else(know_complete, der_eu_know_dk, NA)
  ) |>
  select(-know_complete)

eu25games2019_selected <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  mutate(
    q_risk_taking = scale_point(q_risk_taking),
    q_future_discount = scale_point(q_future_discount)
  ) |>
  left_join(know_scores, by = c("meta_wave", "meta_pid")) |>
  select(-all_of(vars_know))

stopifnot(
  # parse lost nothing
  all(
    is.na(eu25games2019_clean2$q_risk_taking) ==
      is.na(eu25games2019_selected$q_risk_taking)
  ),
  all(
    is.na(eu25games2019_clean2$q_future_discount) ==
      is.na(eu25games2019_selected$q_future_discount)
  ),
  all(between(eu25games2019_selected$q_risk_taking, 1, 7), na.rm = TRUE),
  all(between(eu25games2019_selected$der_eu_know_correct, 0, 4), na.rm = TRUE)
)

vars_post_final <- c(vars_post_game, "der_eu_know_correct", "der_eu_know_dk")
```

# Missingness rule {#sec-missing}

The paper dropped every pre-game item with at least 26% missing values and kept everything below.
Pooled missing shares can hide a different problem: an item that was never fielded in some country.
The four economic-evaluation items are absent in Czechia and Italy, and satisfaction with democracy is absent in Czechia's wave 3.
Pooled, these items are only about 5–13% missing, so a pooled cutoff alone would keep them, and listwise deletion would then remove whole countries from the sample.

The post-game items therefore pass two steps, after backfill:

1. **Fielding gap.** Drop an item if it is more than 90% missing in any country-wave. Missingness at that level means the item was not asked, not that respondents declined to answer.
2. **Item nonresponse.** Apply the paper's pooled 25% cutoff to the remaining items.

The two kinds of missingness separate cleanly.
Fielding gaps are 100% missing in the affected cells.
Ordinary item nonresponse peaks at about a third of a country-wave (left-right self-placement in Latvia's wave 3).
Missing shares are computed among the wave-2/3 rows of respondents who played the games, because these are the rows that enter the analysis.
The pre-game decisions are kept exactly as in the paper.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-missing
vars_na_check <- c(
  vars_pre_game,
  vars_post_final,
  "q_rural_urban",
  "q_edu_age_stop"
)
game_rows <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  filter(meta_wave %in% c(2, 3), !is.na(cj_dict1_pl2))

# worst country-wave cell
na_cell_max <- game_rows |>
  summarise(
    across(all_of(vars_na_check), ~ mean(is.na(.x))),
    .by = c(meta_country, meta_wave)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(vars_na_check), names_to = "variable") |>
  summarise(
    na_max_cell = max(value),
    worst_cell = paste(meta_country[which.max(value)], meta_wave[which.max(value)]),
    .by = variable
  )

na_share <- game_rows |>
  summarise(across(all_of(vars_na_check), ~ mean(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "na_share") |>
  left_join(na_cell_max, by = "variable") |>
  mutate(
    set = if_else(variable %in% vars_post_final, "post-game (new)", "v1.0.0"),
    decision = case_when(
      variable %in% vars_pre_dropped ~ "dropped (v1.0.0)",
      set == "v1.0.0" ~ "kept (v1.0.0)",
      na_max_cell > 0.9 ~ "dropped (fielding gap)",
      na_share > 0.25 ~ "dropped (> 25% NA)",
      .default = "kept"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(set, desc(na_max_cell))

na_share |>
  mutate(across(
    c(na_share, na_max_cell),
    ~ scales::percent(.x, accuracy = 0.1)
  )) |>
  kable(
    caption = "Missing share after backfill among game players (pooled and worst country-wave), and decision."
  )

vars_post_kept <- na_share |>
  filter(set == "post-game (new)", decision == "kept") |>
  pull(variable)

# sanity: paper's split reproduced
stopifnot(
  all(
    na_share$na_share[na_share$decision == "kept (v1.0.0)"] <= 0.25
  )
)
```

# Listwise deletion and reshape {#sec-long}

```{r}
#| label: listwise
eu25_long_ext <- eu25games2019_selected |>
  select(-all_of(vars_pre_dropped)) |>
  select(-all_of(setdiff(vars_post_final, vars_post_kept))) |>
  na.omit() |>
  to_long()

# respondent-waves and persons
n_rw_v1 <- nrow(distinct(eu25_long_v1, meta_pid, meta_wave))
n_rw_ext <- nrow(distinct(eu25_long_ext, meta_pid, meta_wave))
n_pid_v1 <- n_distinct(eu25_long_v1$meta_pid)
n_pid_ext <- n_distinct(eu25_long_ext$meta_pid)
cat(sprintf(
  "Respondent-waves: v1.0.0 = %s, extended = %s (dropped %.1f%%).\nPersons: v1.0.0 = %s, extended = %s (dropped %.1f%%).\n",
  format(n_rw_v1, big.mark = ","),
  format(n_rw_ext, big.mark = ","),
  100 * (n_rw_v1 - n_rw_ext) / n_rw_v1,
  format(n_pid_v1, big.mark = ","),
  format(n_pid_ext, big.mark = ","),
  100 * (n_pid_v1 - n_pid_ext) / n_pid_v1
))

stopifnot(
  # six rounds per respondent-wave
  nrow(eu25_long_ext) == 6 * n_rw_ext,
  # strict subset of v1.0.0
  all(unique(eu25_long_ext$meta_pid) %in% unique(eu25_long_v1$meta_pid)),
  # no country lost
  setequal(unique(eu25_long_ext$meta_country), unique(eu25_long_v1$meta_country)),
  !anyNA(eu25_long_ext$cj_rel),
  !anyNA(select(eu25_long_ext, all_of(vars_post_kept)))
)
```

## Who is dropped? {#sec-attrition}

The extended sample is a subset of the v1.0.0 sample.
The unit is the respondent-wave: a panelist who played in both waves 2 and 3 contributes two sets of six rounds.
The table compares retained and dropped respondent-waves on the numeric pre-game items.
Small differences mean the extended results are comparable to the paper's.

The attrition is selective.
Most dropped respondent-waves answered "don't know" on left-right self-placement (`q_lr_self`), the item with the most nonresponse that is kept.
Dropped respondents report lower understanding of EU politics, are younger, and feel less attached to Europe and the EU.
The extended sample therefore leans toward respondents who can place themselves politically.
`11_grf_fit_ext.qmd` separates this sample shift from the added covariates by also fitting the paper's covariate set on the extended sample.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-attrition
rw_ext <- distinct(eu25_long_ext, meta_pid, meta_wave) |>
  mutate(in_ext = TRUE)
resp_v1 <- eu25_long_v1 |>
  distinct(meta_pid, meta_wave, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  left_join(rw_ext, by = c("meta_pid", "meta_wave")) |>
  mutate(in_ext = coalesce(in_ext, FALSE))

resp_v1 |>
  select(in_ext, where(is.numeric) & starts_with("q_")) |>
  pivot_longer(-in_ext, names_to = "variable") |>
  summarise(mean = mean(value), sd = sd(value), .by = c(variable, in_ext)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = in_ext, values_from = c(mean, sd)) |>
  mutate(std_diff = (mean_TRUE - mean_FALSE) / sd_TRUE) |>
  select(
    variable,
    mean_retained = mean_TRUE,
    mean_dropped = mean_FALSE,
    std_diff
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(std_diff))) |>
  kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Pre-game items: retained vs. dropped v1.0.0 respondents (standardized difference)."
  )

resp_v1 |>
  count(meta_country, in_ext) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = in_ext, values_from = n, names_prefix = "in_ext_") |>
  mutate(share_retained = in_ext_TRUE / (in_ext_TRUE + in_ext_FALSE)) |>
  arrange(share_retained) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Share of v1.0.0 respondents retained, by country.")
```

# Contamination check {#sec-contamination}

In each wave a respondent saw a random number of Muslim profiles across the six game rounds, and then answered that wave's post-game items.
If a post-game item responds to that exposure, the experiment itself shifted it, and CATEs split by the item mix effect modification with the effect of the game.
Exposure is randomized, so a regression of the item on the number of Muslim profiles seen identifies that shift.
The unit is the respondent-wave.
Each item is standardized, so the coefficient is the change in SD units per additional Muslim profile.
Country fixed effects absorb the country-specific design.
Standard errors are clustered by person, because some panelists appear in both waves.
Pre-game items serve as a placebo: they were measured before the games, so their coefficients should be null.
p-values are Holm-adjusted within each set.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-contamination
resp_ext <- eu25_long_ext |>
  mutate(muslim = cj_rel == "muslim") |>
  summarise(
    n_muslim = sum(muslim),
    across(
      c(meta_country, where(is.numeric) & starts_with(c("q_", "der_eu"))),
      first
    ),
    .by = c(meta_pid, meta_wave)
  )

stopifnot(nrow(resp_ext) == n_rw_ext, all(between(resp_ext$n_muslim, 0, 6)))

items_numeric <- resp_ext |>
  select(where(is.numeric) & starts_with(c("q_", "der_eu"))) |>
  names()

contamination <- map(items_numeric, function(v) {
  f <- reformulate(c("n_muslim", "meta_country"), response = "y_std")
  m <- lm(f, data = mutate(resp_ext, y_std = as.numeric(scale(.data[[v]]))))
  # person-clustered SE
  vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = ~meta_pid)
  lmtest::coeftest(m, vcov. = vc) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    filter(term == "n_muslim") |>
    mutate(variable = v)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(
    set = if_else(variable %in% vars_post_kept, "post-game (new)", "v1.0.0")
  ) |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p.value, method = "holm"), .by = set) |>
  mutate(flag = set == "post-game (new)" & p_holm < 0.05) |>
  select(set, variable, estimate, std.error, p.value, p_holm, flag) |>
  arrange(set, p.value)

contamination |>
  kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Standardized item on number of Muslim profiles seen (country FE). Holm-adjusted within set."
  )

cat("Flagged post-game items:", sum(contamination$flag), "\n")
```

# Variable dictionary {#sec-dict}

One row per respondent-level variable in the extended `X`.
`construct` groups items for construct-level summaries.
`high_means` gives the direction of the raw coding, which several batteries reverse (e.g. 1 = "tend to trust").
`timing` records when the item was asked relative to the games.
`q_rural_urban` and `q_edu_age_stop` are post-game demographics that the paper already used as stable background characteristics.

```{r}
#| label: var-dict
var_dict_ext <- tribble(
  ~variable                  , ~construct                   , ~high_means                     ,
  "q_gender"                 , "Demographics"               , "categorical"                   ,
  "q_age"                    , "Demographics"               , "older"                         ,
  "q_religion"               , "Demographics"               , "categorical"                   ,
  "q_class"                  , "Demographics"               , "categorical"                   ,
  "q_rural_urban"            , "Demographics"               , "categorical"                   ,
  "q_edu_age_stop"           , "Demographics"               , "longer education"              ,
  "q_identity_country"       , "Attachment"                 , "less attached"                 ,
  "q_identity_eu"            , "Attachment"                 , "less attached"                 ,
  "q_identity_europe"        , "Attachment"                 , "less attached"                 ,
  "q_eu_efficacy_understand" , "EU efficacy"                , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_pop_reps"               , "Populism"                   , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_pop_goodevil"           , "Populism"                   , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_pop_compromise"         , "Populism"                   , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_party_harm"             , "Populism"                   , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_people_incompetent"     , "Technocracy"                , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_tech_experts"           , "Technocracy"                , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_tech_leaders"           , "Technocracy"                , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_dem_compromise"         , "Pluralism"                  , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_dem_listen"             , "Pluralism"                  , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_eu_longterm"            , "EU responsiveness"          , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_eu_responsive"          , "EU responsiveness"          , "more agree"                    ,
  "q_eu_imp_nat_econ"        , "EU evaluation"              , "more negative"                 ,
  "q_eu_imp_nat_cul"         , "EU evaluation"              , "more negative"                 ,
  "q_eu_imp_nat_pol"         , "EU evaluation"              , "more negative"                 ,
  "q_eu_abolish"             , "EU evaluation"              , "more agree (abolish)"          ,
  "q_eu_satisfaction"        , "EU evaluation"              , "more satisfied"                ,
  "q_nat_int"                , "Political interest"         , "more interested"               ,
  "q_eu_int"                 , "Political interest"         , "more interested"               ,
  "q_nativ_econ"             , "Nativism"                   , "more nativist"                 ,
  "q_nativ_cult"             , "Nativism"                   , "more nativist"                 ,
  "q_eu_informed_com"        , "Informed about EU"          , "less informed"                 ,
  "q_eu_informed_cou"        , "Informed about EU"          , "less informed"                 ,
  "q_eu_informed_ep"         , "Informed about EU"          , "less informed"                 ,
  "q_eu_informed_cjeu"       , "Informed about EU"          , "less informed"                 ,
  "q_eu_trust_com"           , "Trust in EU institutions"   , "less trust"                    ,
  "q_eu_trust_cou"           , "Trust in EU institutions"   , "less trust"                    ,
  "q_eu_trust_ep"            , "Trust in EU institutions"   , "less trust"                    ,
  "q_eu_trust_cjeu"          , "Trust in EU institutions"   , "less trust"                    ,
  "q_cjeu_abolish"           , "CJEU evaluation"            , "more agree (abolish)"          ,
  "q_cjeu_satisfaction"      , "CJEU evaluation"            , "more satisfied"                ,
  "q_eval_econ_eur"          , "Economic evaluation"        , "worse"                         ,
  "q_eval_econ_nat"          , "Economic evaluation"        , "worse"                         ,
  "q_eval_fin_household"     , "Economic evaluation"        , "worse"                         ,
  "q_eval_job"               , "Economic evaluation"        , "worse"                         ,
  "q_satis_demo_nat"         , "Satisfaction with democracy", "less satisfied"                ,
  "q_satis_demo_eu"          , "Satisfaction with democracy", "less satisfied"                ,
  "q_lr_self"                , "Ideology"                   , "more right"                    ,
  "q_euint_self"             , "Ideology"                   , "more pro-integration"          ,
  "q_risk_taking"            , "Risk and time preferences"  , "more risk-taking"              ,
  "q_future_discount"        , "Risk and time preferences"  , "more patient"                  ,
  "q_occ_current"            , "Occupation"                 , "categorical"                   ,
  "der_eu_know_correct"      , "EU knowledge"               , "more correct"                  ,
  "der_eu_know_dk"           , "EU knowledge"               , "more don't know"
) |>
  mutate(
    in_v1 = !(variable %in% vars_post_final),
    timing = if_else(
      in_v1 & !(variable %in% c("q_rural_urban", "q_edu_age_stop")),
      "pre-game",
      "post-game"
    ),
    note = case_when(
      variable %in% c("q_cjeu_abolish", "q_cjeu_satisfaction") ~
        "W3: asked after a randomized CJEU text experiment",
      startsWith(variable, "der_eu_know") ~
        "wave-specific items, scored per wave",
      .default = NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(select(contamination, variable, p_holm, flag), by = "variable") |>
  mutate(contamination_flag = coalesce(flag, FALSE)) |>
  select(-flag) |>
  # keep only variables in X
  filter(variable %in% names(eu25_long_ext))

# every respondent variable documented
resp_vars_ext <- eu25_long_ext |>
  select(starts_with("q_"), starts_with("der_eu_know")) |>
  names()
stopifnot(setequal(resp_vars_ext, var_dict_ext$variable))

var_dict_ext |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Respondent-level variables in the extended analysis.")
```
